Find the measure of angle $A$ given that $m∠B=m∠C.$
question.worked_solution:
Using $m∠B=m∠C,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠B & =m∠C \\ z+{10}^{∘} & =2z \\ z & ={10}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, substituting $z={10}^{∘}$ in the expression for $m∠C,$ we get

$$
m∠C=2({10}^{∘})={20}^{∘}.
$$

Now, we can find $m∠A$ using the fact that the internal angles of any triangle sum to ${180}^{∘}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠C & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠A+2m∠C & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠A+2\cdot {20}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠A+{40}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠A & ={140}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
